Material Synthesis: All reagents were received from Sigma-Aldrich and used without further purification

Preparation of balanced amorphous Cu interface: The balanced amorphous Cu interface was prepared by chemical etching and galvanic Cu regrowth. In brief, a commercial Cu foil (99.97%, 9 μm) was firstly washed in 1 M HCl solution for about 20 minutes to remove the oxide layer, and then washed with acetone, ethanol, and deionized (DI) water to remove the organic substances for a clean surface. This sample was named as normal Cu.

After that, the fresh and clean Cu foil was fully immersed in a typical APS solution (0.18 g (NH4)2S2O8 and 0.6 g KOH dissolved in 30 ml DI water) for 8 minutes’ etching[1], and then transferred into 1 M HCl solution again for the removal of newly formed oxide layer. It could be observed that the color of normal Cu foil turned black during the etching process, and then became dark red in the acid solution. After washed with DI water, this sample was named as etched Cu.

Based on the etched Cu sample, coin-type full cell or the expanded version of pouch cell was assembled using Zn foil (99.99%, 100 μm) and the etched Cu as electrodes and 2 M ZnSO4 as electrolyte. After performing a zinc plating/stripping process on etched Cu at parameters of 15 mA cm−2 / 1 mAh cm−2 with a cut off voltage of −0.3 V, some zinc residue could be observed at the etched Cu surface. Then the stripped Cu sample was put into a solution of 1 M H2SO4 and 6 mM CuSO4 for galvanic replacement

Then the pH of the above solution was adjusted to 3 by adding dilute HCl and stirring for 30 min. DFT simulations were performed using the Castep program package Materials Studio 2020. The exchange-correlate interaction was described by generalized gradient approximation (GGA) with the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) function. The plane wave basis was set with an energy cut-off of 600 eV for all structural optimizations and self-consistent calculations. The slabs were relaxed until the total energy differences were lower than 1.0 × 10–5 eV per atom and the atomic force smaller than –0.02 eV Å–1
